name: Valentina Villa
life: “I still remember my daughter editing my telling of a bedtime story.” People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Valentina by a small Wednesday habit. Valentina usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I was afraid my daughter would believe the ending. She brought me a pencil and asked for my version.
appearance: Valentina is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve, Valentina leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations when listening.
personality: Valentina prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To write a version the daughter knows came from home.
family: Parker Gao is Valentina’s second cousin. Valentina remembers the birthdays. Parker asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The driving lesson fund*, Parker says, “I have the best reason and the worst eyesight.”
connections: Melanie Breen. They compare a name that changed in public with a story a parent wants to correct in private.
